coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 10 units (the domain directory itself plus 9 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md), 58 files total — exactly matching the expected 10 units / 58 files. Every file in every unit was read in full (Related Specs / Constrained by link-only sections excluded from analysis as pure cross-reference lists). Scoring dimensions: Persona Specificity (2) and Competitive Positioning (6) are N/A across all units — personas are owned by meta/personas.md and explicitly 'referenced, never redefined' in every Role Matrix, and competitive positioning belongs to meta/competitive-landscape.md. Dimensions 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 are applicable to every unit, giving 6 applicable checkpoints per unit and 60 overall. Two cross-checks were run against files outside the domain but inside the ideation tree (moscow-ledger.md, to confirm the MoSCoW stage has completed and produced tiering rows) — this is the thing under audit, not an audit artifact. No file under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ other than this output path was opened.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether an RSVP carries a party-size (+N guests), how many admission records issue for it, and who those records are keyed to.
findings.claim: 19.11 ratifies two decisions that cannot both hold for a group RSVP: D-05 makes the cap count heads rather than RSVPs (with an edge case explicitly contemplating one person RSVPing for six), while D-06/DT-03 make the RSVP idempotent per Fan and key the admission record to the Fan's identity, one head per person. D-02 additionally requires every admission to be a real scannable record. An implementer must invent whether a party-size field exists, how many records issue, and how five unidentified guests scan at the door.
findings.evidence: 19.11-rsvp-free-private-event-admission.md:56 — "|Someone RSVPs for 6|Free events attract inflated party sizes|Cap counts heads, not RSVPs (D-05)|"; :57 — "|Same Fan RSVPs twice (double-tap, two devices, re-opened link)|One human, one admission record — the second tap is idempotent, not a second head against the cap|"; :116 D-05 — "The cap counts heads, not RSVPs"; :117 D-06 — "RSVP is idempotent per Fan and self-releasable — one head per person, one-tap 'can't make it' returns the seat"; :93 DT-03 — "the admission record is keyed to the Fan's identity (D-11: fans are real users, not CRM rows), so a repeat RSVP resolves to the same record rather than a new head against the cap"; :113 D-02 — "RSVP issues a real admission record that scans, counts and closes like a ticket".

findings.forcedInvention: Whether a companion ticket carries the ordinary per-ticket booking fee or none at all.
findings.claim: 19.01.03 and 19.01.05 each claim to author the ratified CX-05 companion-fee resolution and state opposite rules. 19.01.03 (D-06, DT-06, edge case) makes the companion a zero-fee entitlement carrying **no** per-ticket booking fee; 19.01.05 (Behavior, D-05) makes the companion's per-ticket fees **equal** those on a comparable general ticket. The fee engine computes a different charge under each. 19.01.03's own edge-case sentence is additionally self-contradictory: it says the companion carries no per-ticket booking fee and in the same breath that the order is 'identical total structure to a comparable two-ticket general order', which cannot both hold, and it defines the save-time parity check as equality against that two-ticket order.
findings.evidence: 19.01.03-fee-structure-all-in-pricing.md:66 — "a **companion ticket is a zero-fee entitlement** bound to an accessible position ... An accessible position + companion purchased in one order therefore incurs exactly one per-order handling/delivery fee and no per-ticket booking fee on the companion line — identical total structure to a comparable two-ticket general order at the same tier ... Operator sees a parity check in the preview: accessible+companion all-in equals comparable general all-in, or save is blocked"; :117 D-06 — "Companion ticket is a zero-fee entitlement; per-order fees charged once per order; parity enforced at save"; 19.01.05-accessible-seating-companion-tickets.md:27 — "A **companion ticket** is an entitlement attached to an accessible position, priced at the comparable general tier (face value) ... Per-ticket fees on the companion equal those on a comparable general ticket at the same face tier — never a premium."; :110 D-05 — "companion per-ticket fees equal the comparable general tier; enforced at fee-config save".

findings.claim: 19.01.02 anchors the hold-owner pre-release prompts to two different clocks in the same file. Behavior anchors them to the deadline (7 days and 24 hours before it); the Happy Path anchors them to doors (doors − 7 days, doors − 24h) while simultaneously calling them 'relative to each hold's deadline'. Under the file's own default deadline of doors − 14 days, the Happy Path reading fires both prompts a week and thirteen days *after* the auto-release has already happened, which is the precise failure DT-13 designs the prompts to precede.
findings.evidence: 19.01.02-capacity-manifest-allocations-holds.md:68 — "The owner is prompted **7 days and 24 hours before** the deadline, and notified *after* the release, not asked."; :101 — "7. At `doors − 7 days` and `doors − 24h` relative to each hold's deadline, system prompts the hold owner: claim all, claim part, or release."; :65 default deadline — "|Any other hold|**Doors − 14 days**|"; :155 States — "|**Deadline due**|A hold's deadline arrives (or `−7d` / `−24h` prompts fire)|".

findings.claim: 19.01.04's Behavior section asserts as normative that seat maps are a domain 16 room asset, while the same file's own Q-01 records that this exact assertion is wrong because domain 16 declines to carry seat identities or map geometry. The Behavior line carries no marker, so an implementer building the seating model from Behavior sources seat maps from an upstream that does not supply them; the correction lives only in a resolved-question cell and routes to another domain's open question.

findings.claim: Four unresolved open questions in this unit carry 'MoSCoW' as their sole deferral target, but the MoSCoW stage has already run and produced moscow-ledger.md. A deferral to a completed stage is not a deferral target — nothing downstream will pick these up. Two of them (tour-wide on-sale as a first-class object; a dedicated embargo-leak recovery affordance) have no corresponding ledger row at all, so they are now unowned. The tree's own convention is to re-point such questions once the stage completes, which was done elsewhere but missed here.

findings.forcedInvention: Where a show's age restriction comes from when there is no upstream source — whether the Operator must declare it per show, and what a show carries when they do not.
findings.claim: 19.04.04 states in three unmarked normative places that the show's age restriction is sourced from / defaults from / originates in the room's licence in domain 16, while the same file's Q-04 records as RESOLVED that domain 16 carries no audience age restriction at all — its five statutory slots are locked and an audience age restriction is not among them, so 'there is therefore no upstream default to inherit, and the restriction is Operator-declared per show here.' Behavior, Happy Path step 1 and the Cross-Cut note describe an inheritance that cannot exist. The domain index independently confirms the gap lands on nobody.

findings.claim: Two edge cases in this unit are marked with a bare '[PENDING]' carrying no owner and no deferral target, and no open question in either file covers them. One is whether an accessible ticket may be transferred at all (which collides with 19.01.05's no-proof-of-disability posture and its resale-flagging rule); the other is the money-safety case where a face-value-exchange buyer has paid but the transfer failed. Every other deferral in this unit names an owner and a target; these two are orphaned.
